    Empirical (simulated) power - Single-test design

    power.copr.emp.Rd

    Monte Carlo estimate of the probability that both co-primary endpoints are declared significant in a single-test design: the observed sensitivity (specificity) is compared with the fixed minimum acceptable value se.min (sp.min). The tests are the ones assumed by power.copr.test, so the result can be compared directly with the asymptotic power.

    power.copr.emp(
  n_dis,
  n_nondis,
  se.e,
  se.min,
  sp.e,
  sp.min,
  alpha = 0.025,
  ci_method = c("wald", "logit"),
  alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided"),
  n_sim = 10000
)

    Arguments

    n_dis, n_nondis

    Number of diseased and non-diseased individuals.

    se.e

    Sensitivity under the alternative hypothesis.

    se.min

    Sensitivity under the null hypothesis.

    sp.e

    Specificity under the alternative hypothesis.

    sp.min

    Specificity under the null hypothesis.

    alpha

    Type I error level (default 0.025).

    ci_method

    Normal approximation method: "wald" (default) or "logit".

    alternative

    "one.sided" (default) or "two.sided".

    n_sim

    Number of simulation replications.

    Value

    Named numeric vector with the empirical power. se and sp are the proportions of the n_sim replications in which the sensitivity and the specificity endpoint is rejected, respectively. overall is the proportion in which both are rejected. The Monte Carlo standard error of each is at most \(0.5/\sqrt{n_{sim}}\).

    Details

    In each replication the true positives are drawn from \(\mathrm{Bin}\)(n_dis, se.e) and, independently, the true negatives from \(\mathrm{Bin}\)(n_nondis, sp.e), for all n_sim replications at once (no loop). For an observed proportion \(\hat p\) and null value \(p_0\) an endpoint is rejected if $$\sqrt{n}\,(g(\hat p) - g(p_0)) / \sqrt{V_0} > z_{1-\alpha},$$ with \(g\) the identity ("wald") or the logit ("logit"). \(V_0\) is the null variance of \(\sqrt{n}\,g(\hat p)\): \(V_0 = p_0(1-p_0)\) on the Wald scale and \(V_0 = 1/(p_0(1-p_0))\) on the logit scale (the delta-method variance of the logit of a proportion). The Wald version uses the variance under the null and therefore coincides with the Wilson score interval: rejecting is the same as the lower limit of prop.test(x, n, conf.level = 1 - 2 * alpha, correct = FALSE) exceeding \(p_0\).

    See also

    power.copr.test,power.copr.comp.emp

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
power.copr.emp(n_dis = 61, n_nondis = 61,
                    se.e = 0.85, se.min = 0.65,
                    sp.e = 0.85, sp.min = 0.55)
#> overall      se      sp 
#>  0.9651  0.9655  0.9996
